news_drafts.headline: Barnsley forecasts £1.5m overspend as £1.6m borrowing underspend offsets £3.1m service pressures
news_drafts.lead:
Barnsley Council is forecasting a £1.5m overspend on its day-to-day budget for 2026/27, according to the first-quarter finance report going to Cabinet on 7 October. Services are forecast to overspend by £3.1m as at the end of June. That is partly offset by a one-off £1.6m underspend on corporate budgets, from lower borrowing costs and extra investment income.

Adult social care accounts for £1.5m of the service overspend, and children's social care and the Place directorate £0.9m each. In children's services, 61 children are in external residential placements, against 50 a year earlier, and 93 are with independent fostering agencies, against 76. The report puts each additional residential placement at more than £0.4m a year. A sufficiency strategy approved in April includes three council-led children's homes, but implementation is delayed. Agency staff spending is forecast at £4.3m, against more than £10.6m last year, which the report says shows the reduction programme "starting to have the desired effect".

The council's medium-term financial strategy, its plan showing the gap between expected spending and income, now puts the gap at about £31m to 2029/30. In February it was £23m to 2028/29. The £31m is before the first-quarter pressures, which would take it to £34m unless offset. The 2026/27 budget already uses £4.2m of strategic reserves, money set aside for the council's priorities. The report says further deterioration would mean using reserves earmarked for other priorities and could require savings beyond the £30m already needed.

Separately, the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, is forecast to be £13.4m overspent in 2026/27, mainly on high needs, the funding for children with special educational needs. The report expects the deficit to rise by a further £14.6m in 2027/28. Government has extended the statutory override, a rule keeping such deficits off the main balance sheet, until April 2028, but has not published detail on funding for deficits beyond 2025/26.

Capital spending, on things that last, has £21.2m slipping into later years, mostly sustainable transport schemes. Business rates collection is forecast at 96.69% against a 98% target.

news_drafts.headline: Barnsley Council accepts electronic records gap it cannot afford to fix
news_drafts.lead: Barnsley Council's governance and compliance board has formally agreed to accept a risk in electronic records management, determining that available solutions to fix the problem are too expensive to implement. Staff continue reviewing paper records for disposal, but the electronic records management issue remains unresolved. The board's decision reflects resource constraints the council faces in balancing competing budget demands across its services. Electronic records management has not been prioritised for spending at this time.

findings.paper_title: 20261109 - NAC Item 5 - Commissioning and Finance Update
findings.headline: Two North Area Council commissions, the Health and Wellbeing Fund and the Youth Resilience Fund, are both scheduled to end in 2027, four months apart.
findings.detail: The Health and Wellbeing Fund ends on 30 June 2027 and the Youth Resilience Fund on 31 October 2027. The paper recommends workshops to plan successor arrangements, and warns that deferring them could create overlapping commissions and strain resources.
findings.matters: A committee facing two funding cliffs close together must decide whether to re-procure, extend or stop each service, which is a planning issue any council with time-limited grant commissions will face.
findings.figures: £104,133.50 Youth Resilience Fund 2026/27; £38,885.05 Health and Wellbeing 2026/27; 2 commissions ending within 4 months
findings.quote: In 2027, 2 commissions are scheduled to end within 4 months of one another

findings.paper_title: 20261109 - NAC Item 5 - Commissioning and Finance Update
findings.headline: The Environmental Caretakers' contingency for 2025/26 was allocated £22,229.00 and actually spent £1,563.35.
findings.detail: The paper lists the contingency being not fully utilised as the main reason for the 2025/26 underspend. The core Environmental Contract also spent £107,022.51 against £111,143.00 allocated.
findings.matters: A contingency that is largely unspent shows how a reserve-style allocation can sit idle in a year when the underlying service is not drawing on it.
findings.figures: £22,229.00 allocated contingency 2025/26; £1,563.35 actual contingency spend 2025/26; £111,143.00 Environmental Contract allocated 2025/26; £107,022.51 Environmental Contract actual 2025/26
findings.quote: Environmental Caretakers’ contingency allocation not fully utilised.

findings.paper_title: 20261109 - NAC Item 5 - Commissioning and Finance Update
findings.headline: The Area Council's 2026/27 unallocated spend is £38,563 against allocated expenditure and £44,904 against forecast expenditure.
findings.detail: The paper says this headroom gives the Area Council flexibility to invest in further provision. It also suggests ring-fencing part of it to maintain current service levels in 2027/28 and beyond.
findings.matters: A committee deciding whether to hold headroom back for future years, rather than spend it, faces the same choice finance directors face with any unallocated reserve.
findings.figures: £38,563 unallocated against allocated; £44,904 unallocated against forecast
findings.quote: The unallocated spend for the 2026/27 financial year is £38,563 against allocated and £44,904 against forecasted expenditure respectively.

findings.paper_title: 20261109 - NAC Item 5 - Commissioning and Finance Update
findings.headline: The Area Council's 2026/27 allocated and forecast budgets are over the £400,000 base budget, and the paper says carry-forward is sufficient to absorb the excess.
findings.detail: The paper states that the Area Council is financially committed over the base budget for 2026/27. It identifies the ongoing risk that service costs are rising while budgets remain static.
findings.matters: This shows a council committee relying on carry-forward to meet a commitment above its recurring base budget, with the paper flagging rising costs against static budgets as an ongoing risk.
findings.quote: The allocated and forecasted budgets indicate that the Area Council is financially committed over the base budget for 2026/27. The carry-forward from previous years is sufficient to absorb this.

findings.paper_title: 20261109 - NAC Item 5 - Commissioning and Finance Update
findings.headline: The Area Council's 2026/27 total budget is £469,757, made up of a £400,000 base budget plus £69,757 from carry-forward and the 2025/26 underspend.
findings.detail: The carry-forward from previous years is £56,213, and the 2025/26 underspend adds to it. The paper states the combined figure as the total budget available for 2026/27.
findings.matters: It shows a committee drawing on accumulated carry-forward to sit above its annual base budget, which is a pattern other councils' finance teams will recognise.
findings.figures: £400,000 base budget; £56,213 carry-forward; £69,757 carry-forward and underspend together; £469,757 total budget for 2026/27
findings.quote: The carry forward and underspend together total £69,757 which, in addition to the base budget of £400,000, equates to a total budget of £469,757 for the 2026/27 financial year.

daily_post.headline: Network Optimisation project approved to proceed to procurement targeting £150,000 recurring annual efficiency, intended to fit within existing £781,000 budget with explicit contingency to bring revised financial case back if costs exceed envelope.
daily_post.lead: The contingency language indicates cost uncertainty on a material project; any budget pressure would add to the council's overall financial pressures and the £31M gap.
